The paper proposes a Toeplitz-based lens that separates positional encodings into additive mechanisms (a static translation-invariant bias added to logits) and multiplicative ones (RoPE, a Toeplitz kernel applied via Hadamard product to all content interactions), and uses two synthetic tasks to argue that RoPE's multiplicative coupling causes a 'single-head deposit pattern' in which shallow-layer positional logic collapses into one attention head. The phenomenon is interesting and the ablation suite (head-wise zeroing, hybrid Absolute+RoPE, RoPE-on-k-heads, MLA, layer-wise p_i removal) is thoughtfully constructed, which is the manuscript's main strength. However, the evidence base is two bespoke synthetic tasks on a single 6-layer model with no real-data or scale validation, the statistical reporting is a single sentence ('variance less than 5%') with no per-condition error bars or tests, the theory rests on informally stated assumptions with proofs deferred to an unavailable appendix, and several textual claims conflict with the reported numbers. As submitted the central claim that the deposit pattern is an intrinsic property of RoPE that explains its practical performance paradox is under-supported.
